corrected_content.problem:
$${∬}_{D}\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAAAA}}\,\text{d}A,\,D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le \pi \}$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface $\mathbf{r}(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\hspace{0.222em}2u\operatorname{sin}v,\hspace{0.222em}u\operatorname{cos}v⟩$ for $0\le u\le 2$ and $0\le v\le \pi .$ What is the missing expression?
corrected_content.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\hspace{0.167em}\text{d}S={∬}_{D}‖{\mathbf{r}}_{u}^{'}\times {\mathbf{r}}_{v}^{'}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{r}}_{u}^{'} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\hspace{0.222em}\frac{∂y}{∂u},\hspace{0.222em}\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\hspace{0.222em}\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u\operatorname{sin}v),\hspace{0.222em}\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{cos}v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\hspace{0.222em}2\operatorname{sin}v,\hspace{0.222em}\operatorname{cos}v⟩ \\ {\mathbf{r}}_{v}^{'} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\hspace{0.222em}\frac{∂y}{∂v},\hspace{0.222em}\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\hspace{0.222em}\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u\operatorname{sin}v),\hspace{0.222em}\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{cos}v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\hspace{0.222em}2u\operatorname{cos}v,\hspace{0.222em}-u\operatorname{sin}v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{r}}_{u}^{'}\times {\mathbf{r}}_{v}^{'} & =\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 2u & 2\operatorname{sin}v & \operatorname{cos}v \\ 0 & 2u\operatorname{cos}v & -u\operatorname{sin}v\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}2\operatorname{sin}v & \operatorname{cos}v \\ 2u\operatorname{cos}v & -u\operatorname{sin}v\end{vmatrix},\hspace{0.222em}-\begin{vmatrix}2u & \operatorname{cos}v \\ 0 & -u\operatorname{sin}v\end{vmatrix},\hspace{0.222em}\begin{vmatrix}2u & 2\operatorname{sin}v \\ 0 & 2u\operatorname{cos}v\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨-2u{\operatorname{sin}}^{2}v-2u{\operatorname{cos}}^{2}v,\hspace{0.222em}2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}v,\hspace{0.222em}4{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}v⟩ \\  & =⟨-2u,\hspace{0.222em}2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}v,\hspace{0.222em}4{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}v⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{\mathbf{r}}_{u}^{'}\times {\mathbf{r}}_{v}^{'}‖ & =‖⟨-2u,\hspace{0.222em}2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}v,\hspace{0.222em}4{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}v⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(2u)^{2}+(2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}v)^{2}+(4{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}v)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{u}^{2}+4{u}^{4}{\operatorname{sin}}^{2}v+16{u}^{4}{\operatorname{cos}}^{2}v} \\  & =\sqrt{4{u}^{2}+4{u}^{4}({\operatorname{sin}}^{2}v+{\operatorname{cos}}^{2}v)+12{u}^{4}{\operatorname{cos}}^{2}v} \\  & =\sqrt{4{u}^{2}+4{u}^{4}+12{u}^{4}{\operatorname{cos}}^{2}v} \\  & =\sqrt{4{u}^{2}(1+{u}^{2}+3{u}^{2}{\operatorname{cos}}^{2}v)} \\  & =\sqrt{4{u}^{2}}\sqrt{1+{u}^{2}+3{u}^{2}{\operatorname{cos}}^{2}v} \\  & =2u\sqrt{1+{u}^{2}+3{u}^{2}{\operatorname{cos}}^{2}v}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $\sqrt{{u}^{2}}=u$ since $u\ge 0$ on $D.$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\hspace{0.167em}\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{\mathbf{r}}_{u}^{'}\times {\mathbf{r}}_{v}^{'}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}{\color{blue}2u\sqrt{1+{u}^{2}+3{u}^{2}{\operatorname{cos}}^{2}v}}\hspace{0.222em}\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$
